items.review_rationale: Read domination of local subrings of one common field through inclusion and contraction of the larger ring's maximal ideal; kept local-ring maximal ideals distinct.

references.phrase: local ring A and local ring B

references.context: Inclusion as subrings of a fixed ambient field, preserving identities.
The maximal ideal of B pulled back along inclusion A→B equals the maximal ideal of A.

references.disposition: B dominates A only when B extends A and the maximal ideals are compatible; ordinary abstract ring isomorphism does not establish it.

items.review_rationale: Read valuation ring as an integral domain with its own fraction field satisfying reciprocal membership for every nonzero fraction; distinguished fractions in the field from arbitrary ring elements.

references.context: Element x≠0 of the fraction field of V, for which both x and x^{-1} are well-defined.

references.phrase: x or x inverse belongs to V
references.context: For each nonzero fraction either x lies in V or the reciprocal lies in V, inclusive or; both may lie in V for units.

references.disposition: This is an equivalent characterization independent of a chosen explicit valuation map, not a discrete value-group hypothesis.
